# Tinkrum app rules: how to build what people ask for

A companion to the Tinkrum app-file guide (tinkrum-app-guide.md). Read the rule you need when an app calls for something the guide and the patterns don't show: totals and streaks from a linked table (rule 42), dates that repeat (43, 47, 50), one-tap buttons on entries (44, 61, 62, 63), grouping and calendars (45), progress or a running timer on a list row (46), a page for one entry (48, 58), days left until a date (32), reminders (35, 59, 60, 66), tabs and time ranges on a page (56, 65), the entry form's layout (64), fixed zones and block sizes (55, 67).

These rules come from Tink, the assistant inside Tinkrum, which changes an app one operation at a time: where a rule names an operation (`addData`, `addContainer`, `addTool`, `updateData`…), write the finished object into the file instead, as the guide's "How to read the reference" says. Rules about Tink's conversation and about the whole phone are left out, so the numbers have gaps: when a rule mentions one that is not here, ignore that mention.

## Rules
10. Readability is enforced: body text must have at least 4.5:1 contrast against both background and surface (surfaceText, if set, is what is checked against surface), in every mode the theme can show ("system" means both light and dark). When the user wants a dark or colored background, set colors.background, colors.surface and colors.text together (e.g. dark navy #10233F / #18304F / #F5F7FA), or simply switch mode to "dark" if they just want dark mode. Don't change colors they didn't mention. A dark background with light cards (or the other way round): also set colors.surfaceText, the text color on cards, so text only has to read on the background and surfaceText on the cards (e.g. dark green #0B3D2E / cream #F5EFE0 / text #F5EFE0 / surfaceText #2A2420).
13. Layout: to put blocks side by side or in a grid, add a group (show.layout "row" or "grid") and moveContainer the existing blocks into it with parent, rather than recreating them. A group may hold one more group (e.g. a card with two numbers side by side and a button below), never deeper.
32. Formula fields (computed, R10). Conditions ("10% off when the total is 100 or more", "bonus 50 if the rating is 5"): the expression may also use if(left OP right, a, b) where OP is one of > < >= <= = and a, b are arithmetic (if may be nested). Comparisons exist only as the first part of if; there are no other words, functions (except those in this rule), text comparisons or logic operators (and / or): nest if instead. Example: "if({total} >= 100, {total} * 0.9, {total})". Dates ("days left until the due date", "how many days it was late"): a date field {fieldId} and the word today are dates; days(from, to) gives the number of days from one to the other (to − from, negative when to is earlier), and two dates can be compared in if(). Dates can't be added, subtracted or multiplied directly, and the formula must give a number: "days left" is "days(today, {due})" with unit "days" and decimals 0. When a date field is empty the formula has no value. More: min(a, b, …) and max(a, b, …) (2-10 parts), round(x) or round(x, digits 0-4) and abs(x), on numbers. hours(from, to) and minutes(from, to) give the time from one time field to another, or from one datetime field to another (to − from); for two time fields an end earlier than the start is on the next day (22:00 → 06:00 is 8 hours). days() also takes datetime fields. A duration field is its number of minutes ("{break} / 60" is hours). Times and datetimes can't be added or multiplied, and if() compares them only with the same kind. A formula may use other formula fields of the same table, e.g. pay "{worked} * {rate}" where worked is "hours({start}, {end}) - {break} / 60" (decimals 2, unit "h"), but never in a loop that comes back to itself. An expression is at most 500 characters. A checkbox field is 1 when ticked and 0 when not: "still to pay" is "if({paid} = 1, 0, {amount})" or "{amount} * (1 - {paid})". A choice field is the value of the chosen option, so its options need a value (an option {id, label, value}): "cost per year" is "{price} * {cycle}" with options monthly value 12 and yearly value 1; no option chosen, or one without a value, gives no result.
33. Summaries of a table are number and chart blocks (their source is written as in their look docs); you only choose how they are built and never see the values. Totals per category ("how much per category") → a number block with source.group {by: that choice field}: one row per option and a "not set" row. A link field works too (D-336): one row per entry of the linked table, as a summary block of its own. When the value belongs on each entry of that linked table instead ("for each habit show …", a streak on each habit when habits are their own table), it is a rollup field on that table, shown in its list (rule 42), not a number block grouped by the link. A number block can't be grouped by other fields. Charts ("a chart of spending per month", "pie chart by category") → a chart block on the page that shows the table: amounts over time are kind "bar" or "line" grouped by unit, with last = how many recent days / weeks / months (12 for "the last year by month"); shares of a whole are kind "pie" grouped by a choice field. Use aggregate "sum" with the money field for spending, "count" for how many entries; a single total or a per-category list without a picture is a number block. Habits and "how long since" ("days since I last watered each plant", "average cycle length") → a number block with a day-based aggregate: "streak" (current run of days in a row, with the best run under it; today not logged yet does not break it), "daysSince" (days since the latest entry), "avgInterval" (average days between entry days), "distinctDays" (days with at least one entry). One row per habit / plant / car → source.group {by: the choice field that names it} (when they are their own table: the rollup above). "3 times a week" → days {unit: "week", perUnit: 3}. An option meaning "skipped" or "rest day" → days.skip {field, option}: such days neither break nor add. A chart can only use "distinctDays"; the others are number blocks. A goal ("show today's water against a goal of 8 glasses" → sum or count, filter inPeriod "today", goal 8) shows "value / goal" with progress. compare: "previous" ("vs last week") needs exactly one inPeriod filter; it shows the previous value for the same days so far and ↑/↓ with the percent; not for streak, daysSince or avgInterval. One total minus another ("balance = income − spending", "stock = in − out") → source.minus: the block's own total minus that one, which may come from another table; both aggregates count or sum, the same currency, and no group or compare. Without a period filter both totals cover all entries, so money not spent stays counted month after month (a zero-based budget: categories with assignments and spending as linked tables, "available" = a rollup of everything assigned minus a rollup of everything spent, rule 42).
34. Tables that refer to each other ("each order belongs to a client", "link expenses to a trip") → addData {table: the table that points, field: {type: "link", table: the other table}} (the other table must exist; create it first with addData in the same plan, and give it a way to add entries too: its own list with addHere or a form, in next if the plan is function changes). It can be asked in a form and shown as a record block's show.title / subtitles / trailing; filter it only with isEmpty / isNotEmpty (or is "$record" on a page for one entry, rule 48) and never sort by it. A table that other tables link to can't be removed until those link fields are removed: removeData {table, field} them (and take them out of blocks) before removeData {table}. Deleting the linked entry is the user's own action on the page; the link then shows "Deleted entry" until the entry is restored.
35. Reminders ("remind me every day at 9 to log expenses", "remind me 3 days before a bill is due") are local notifications on this device: addTool {tool: Reminder} (the type is under Output; week days: 1 = Monday; before = one notification per entry, days before that date field, its text made on the device from the entry). title is the notification title in the interface language. opens is where tapping it goes: the page that shows that table, or "tool:<id>" for a quick action — it only opens it, the user taps Start; nothing ever runs by itself (R13), so "run X every morning" is still impossible: add a reminder that opens X and say so in a note. Turning one off is updateTool {tool, changes: {enabled: false}}; changing its time is updateTool {tool, changes: {when: the whole new when}}. Existing reminders are in tools[]. Reminders are a function change (rule 26): when one is asked for together with a new table, add it in the same plan as the table, with opens "page:home" if its page doesn't exist yet, because next can't carry it. The app asks for notification permission itself the first time a reminder is on. Reminders for each entry on its own schedule → when {each: {table, field: a schedule field of that table (rule 43; add it first if missing)}, at}: each entry with a rule gets its own notifications on its due days at that time; entries done that day (lastDone) move on to their next date. At most 10 reminders of this kind, apart from the 20 others. The notification shows the entry's title, made on the device (you never see entries); title is a short generic line in the interface language such as "Time to do it" — never an entry's name or content. unless ("don't remind me if I already checked in today") skips a day when that table already has a matching entry in the same day / week / month (date default createdAt) — on the same table only the entry itself counts, with link (a link field of that table pointing to this table) only the entries linked to it (e.g. {table: "check-ins", within: "day", link: "habit"} = "not if already checked in today"). done = the notification's "Done" button (always labelled "Done" in the interface language; a custom label like "Watered" is not possible, say so in a note): one record tool on that entry (rule 44 without as, label or when; table = when.each.table, or the table a create writes; "$row" = this entry, e.g. {do: "create", table: "check-ins", values: {habit: "$row"}}); it only writes the entry, never runs a quick action. snoozeMinutes 5-240 adds a "Remind me later" button. Nothing happens unless the user taps. A reminder some minutes after each new entry ("remind me 10 minutes after I add a task") → when {after: {table}, minutes: 1-1440}: one notification per entry, that many minutes after it was added (only entries added from now on); "minutes before" a date or time is not possible (before counts whole days), say so in a note.
38. Photos and files on entries ("attach receipts to my expenses") → addData {table, field: {type: "file", …}} on that table; one attachment field holds up to 20 files per entry, so add it only when the table has none. The user takes or picks the files in the entry forms (the full editor shows every field; put it in an inline form's ask only when they ask for it on the page). Don't also build an out.addRecord quick action unless they ask for a quick action. You never see, name or choose the files.
40. Times and lengths of time ("log when I start and stop work", "sleep diary") → a time field is a time of day; a datetime field is a date with a time of day: give "when it happened" fields default "now" so a new entry starts at the moment it is added; a duration field is a length of time in minutes, which number blocks and charts can sum and average. Use a plain date field when only the day matters. A datetime field is filtered by its day: inPeriod, or is / gt / lt with a "YYYY-MM-DD" value; a time field is compared with gt / lt and an "HH:mm" value. A chart's source.group.by can be a datetime field.
42. Values from a linked table ("each client's order total" with a categories table, a streak on each habit when habits are their own table that check-ins link to, "stock from in and out movements") → addData {table: the table that shows the value, field}. A lookup copies a field of the entry its link field via picks (an hourly rate onto each work entry; then a formula "{hours} * {rate}" works). A rollup sums up the entries of table whose link field via picks this entry (via is a link field of that table pointing at this table; add it first when it is missing, rule 34): count; sum, avg, min or max of a number, money, rating, duration or formula field; latest (field of the most recent entry by date; without field, that entry's date, e.g. "last time"); or the day-based aggregates of rule 33 with days. filter narrows the entries (a period such as this month is an inPeriod condition). Change since the previous entry ("distance since the last fill-up") → a previous field (date default: the first date field; within = a choice or link field such as the car, to compare only within it); then a formula such as "{odometer} - {prev-odometer}". The first entry has none. Showing these values is a look change for next (rule 26): a list of the table that has them (show.subtitles or trailing), not a number block. All three are computed (R10): never asked in a form; formulas, filters, sorting, number blocks and charts use them like the field they show. At most 3 levels of lookups and rollups on top of each other, never in a loop. When habits are only options of a choice field in one check-in table, keep rule 33 (a number block grouped by it).
43. Things that repeat ("bills on the 1st and 15th", "take vitamins twice a day", "birthdays") → a schedule field {type: "schedule", default?: Rule, lastDone?}: each entry keeps its own rule, which the user sets in the entry form; default is the rule new entries start with (you never set an entry's rule). Rule = {repeat: "daily"} | {repeat: "weekdays", days: [1-7] (1 = Monday, 7 = Sunday)} | {repeat: "times", per: "week"|"twoWeeks"|"month"|"year", count} (any days, count times each period) | {repeat: "monthDays", days: [1-31, or -1 = the last day]} (a day past the end of a month falls on its last day) | {repeat: "interval", every: 1-60} (every N days) | {repeat: "yearly", month: 1-12, day}, each with perDay? (2-20 times a day). "Every N days" and "N times a week" count from when it was last done: add a date (or datetime) field such as "Last watered" and set lastDone to its id, or, when each time is logged as an entry of another table (a check-ins table linked to this one), add a rollup field over those entries (rule 42) and set lastDone to it: then every logged day counts, so "3 times a week" knows how many are done this week; without lastDone, fixed days (Mon/Wed/Fri, the 1st, yearly) are due on those days and "every N days" stays due. Lists show the rule and the next date. Filter {field, op: "due", value: "today" (overdue included) | "overdue" | "thisWeek" (due by the end of this week)}; inPeriod and gt / lt use the next date; sorting by it sorts by next date (overdue first); in a formula it is the next date: days(today, {renews}) is days left (negative when overdue). Reminders for each entry on its own schedule: rule 35.
44. Record tools on blocks (R4, R7, R12): one-tap buttons that change entries ("a +1 water button", "clock in / clock out", "mark as paid", "uncheck everything on the packing list", "Fait" next to each habit) → a button block with tools [one record tool] (no as) instead of opens, or tools with as "button" on a record block (RecordTool and ToolUse under Output). A value can only be an option id (choice), a number (number, money, rating, duration in minutes), true / false (checkbox), "today" (date), "now" (time, datetime) or null (clear); in a create's values a link field may also be "$row" or "$record"; never text: the user types text, so for "a button that adds rent with the name filled in" use ask: "all". On a button block: create adds one entry per tap ("+1 glass of water" = create with glasses 1, and a number block sums today); setAll sets field on every matching entry (the app asks first; at most 200, R8); create with ask: "all" opens the new-entry form with the values already filled in, and the user types the rest (amount, note) and saves ("log a fill-up for this car", "add an order for this customer"; also when a required field needs text) — required fields may stay empty with ask "all". Row buttons on a record block (up to 3; as "button", label ≤20 chars, when?: conditions on the row): set, toggle (a checkbox), increment (number, money or duration), create (a link field to the block's table may be "$row": this row's entry, e.g. "Done" on each habit adds a check-in for it; ask?: "all"), or opens: "record" (the entry's editor) or a page for one entry (rule 48); each row shows the first one whose when matches, e.g. a button block creating {start: "now"} for "Clock in" and on the shifts list {as: "button", label: "Clock out", do: "set", table: "shifts", field: "end", value: "now", when: [{field: "end", op: "isEmpty"}]}. A record tool writes its block's source.table, or (create only) another table whose link field is set to "$row" / "$record" (R12); a button or form block names the table it writes. A create without ask must leave no required field empty (preset it or give the field a default). Nothing runs until the user taps; the user takes a tap back the normal way (untick, edit, delete). They are look changes (rule 26): a new table or field comes first, the buttons go in next.
45. Record views and grouping: every record block groups with source.group, written the same way. A month calendar of entries ("show my workouts on a calendar", "period calendar") → look "calendar": the user moves between months, and tapping a day lists its entries (show.title / subtitles / trailing) below the month; group.by defaults to the first date field; show.color (a choice field, e.g. mood) colors each day by its latest entry's option, otherwise days get darker with more entries; limit is the most entries listed for one day. Use it next to, not instead of, the table's normal list unless the user asks to replace it. A board of columns ("kanban", "move orders from new to shipped") → look "board" with source.group {by: a choice field} (required for a board): one column per option in option order, plus "Not set" for entries without one; limit is per column. Give it the drag tool (see board): the user drags a card to another column (or taps it and picks "Move to…"), which sets the field; without the drag tool the board only shows. If the table already has a choice or link field (priority, project, section), group by it; only if it has none, add one first (rule 26: the field first, the board next). Tasks that are finished by being done (a once schedule, rule 47) never get a status choice with a "done" option: the board shows pending ones (filter {op: "due", value: "pending"}) and finished tasks leave it. Sections in a list ("show the transactions by day") → source.group on a list, cards or checklist: by a choice or link field (one section per option or linked entry, in their order; showEmpty: true also lists sections with nothing in them, like a task app's sections) or by a date, datetime, schedule field or createdAt with unit "day" (default) | "week" | "month" (a schedule groups by its next date, with Overdue first and No date last; sort by the same field so the days come in order); each section has a title with its count and folds when tapped; limit is per section. A board per project with the project's own sections → a sections table (name, a link to the project), a link field on the tasks pointing at sections, and a board grouped by that link: one column per section entry, in the order they were made; on a page for one project (rule 48) add source.group.filter [{field: the sections' project link, op: "is", value: "$record"}] so only that project's sections become columns. Adding right where you look ("add a task on the day I picked in the calendar") → the tool {as: "addHere", do: "create", table, ask: "all", values: "$here"}: each section title, each column, the picked day of a calendar and the bottom of a plain list get an Add that opens the new-entry form with that section's value (an option, a linked entry, the day — a schedule gets once on that day) and the block filter's equal-to conditions (choice, link, checkbox; "$record" on a page for one entry) already filled in. A floating add ("a + button that opens a quick add sheet") → a form block with show.mode "sheet": a round + at the bottom right of the page (one per page, not in a group) opens the form from the bottom, the keyboard's Done adds, and it stays open for the next one; smartDate (rule 49) works there too.
46. Showing a value differently in a record block: show.format on show.trailing. {kind: "elapsed", until?} shows the time from show.trailing (a datetime field or "createdAt", the start) until the datetime field until, or until now while until is empty — a timer that ticks ("how long has this been running", "fasting timer": trailing = the start, until = the end). {kind: "progress", goal, style?: "ring"|"bar"} shows "3 / 5" with a ring (default) or bar: trailing is a number, money, rating, duration, formula or rollup field; goal is a positive number or a number field of the same table (e.g. a rollup "this week" with goal "weekly-goal"). Elapsed and progress never change the stored values.
47. To-dos and one-off things with an optional day ("a task list like Todoist", "renew passport by March", "rappels ponctuels") → a schedule field whose default is {repeat: "once"}: the user picks a day in the form ({repeat: "once", date}) or leaves it without one ("someday"), and can switch any entry to a repeat rule (rule 43), so one field holds one-off and repeating tasks. A once is finished after it is done once (lastDone, rule 43) and then has no next date; filter {op: "due", value: "pending"} keeps everything not finished (repeating entries always stay pending), so "today" = due today, "inbox / all open tasks" = due pending. Mark done with a row button that logs a completion (a completions table linked to the tasks, lastDone = a rollup of its latest date, rule 42; rule 44 create with the link "$row"): that also gives the completed history, "done today" counts and streaks. Don't add a "done" checkbox for repeating things: it can't come back next time. countEarly: true on the schedule field makes doing it early count for the coming time, as to-do apps do (done on Sunday for a Monday task → the Monday after); leave it off for bills, where paying early doesn't skip the next one. Rounding off a to-do app: when the tasks table is made in a function turn, next keeps everything the user asked for the pages (which tasks show, e.g. today's) and adds the done row button, since without it a task can never be finished. Every list and board of the tasks except a completed history filters {field: the schedule, op: "due", value: "pending"} (finished once entries leave; "today" and "overdue" already leave them out), including lists on a page for one entry. Adding subtasks (a parent link to the tasks' own table) also adds two rollups on the tasks over that link (rule 42): count = all subtasks, count with filter due pending = open ones; next (rule 26) then asks to filter {field: parent, op: "isEmpty"} on the lists and boards of top-level tasks and show the counts in their subtitles. A per-entry reminder (rule 35) on tasks that are marked done with a completion gets done = the same create (e.g. {do: "create", table: "completions", values: {task: "$row"}}) and snoozeMinutes 30, so the notification can finish the task.
48. A page for one entry ("open a customer to see their orders", "a task's subtasks") → addContainer {page: {id, title, of: the table whose entries it shows, blocks}}, and set opens: that page id on a record block of that table, so tapping an entry opens the page instead of the editor (the page title shows the entry); a row button {as: "button", label, opens: that page id} opens it too. On that page, "$record" means the entry: filter {field: a link field pointing at the page's table, op: "is", value: "$record"} lists what belongs to it, and create values (buttons, row buttons, forms) can set such a link to "$record" (add a subtask, an order for this customer). A link to its own table works too (parent → subtasks). Such a page gets no nav entry, entry, button or reminder (it doesn't know which entry); it only opens from a record block. A form's create tool may have values: preset values that are not shown, e.g. {"project": "$record"} for a quick add on a project page.
49. Typing a date in the same line ("type 'call mom tomorrow'") → set smartDate {from: the text field, to: a date, datetime or schedule field} on the create tool of a form block whose ask includes that text field. The app recognises dates, times and repeats ("every Monday") on the phone, highlights them and fills the field on save, taking the words out of the text; you never read or parse what users type (D-113). A schedule field gets {repeat: "once", date} or a repeat rule; a date field only takes dates.
50. A time on a schedule ("the dentist on Friday at 3pm") is the user's own: rules take time? "HH:mm" (any rule), entries show "Tomorrow at 15:00" and sort by it within a day, and per-entry reminders (rule 35) fire at the entry's own time, falling back to the reminder's time. You never set an entry's time; smartDate (rule 49) fills it from what the user types. A calendar (rule 45) can group by a schedule field: each entry shows on its coming days (overdue ones on today, finished once entries not at all).
55. Fixed zones: any top-level block on a page may have pin: "top" or pin: "bottom"; it stays in place while the middle of the page scrolls (never inside a group, never a list with show.browse). Set it with addContainer, or updateContainer {page, block, changes: {pin: "top"|"bottom"|null}}. show.browse.pin: true keeps a list's search box, sort and filter chips fixed at the top while the list scrolls (one per page, on a top-level list). When the user wants big floating actions like "scan" with "more" behind an arrow ("floating add button with more options"), use a dial; several ordinary actions keep their blocks. {as: "list"} on a dial needs exactly one top-level list with show.browse on the same page, and a quick action whose first step takes records (rule 54). Nothing on a dial runs by itself; each tool runs when tapped.
56. Time range on a page: when the user wants to switch what a page covers ("let me pick this week or this month"), add ONE period block with only the choices they name (fewer is better: "this month, this week" → options ["thisMonth", "thisWeek"]; add custom: true for "pick my own dates") and set source.period: "page" on EVERY chart and number block already on that page (all of them follow unless the user says one should stay fixed, e.g. "the yearly total stays as it is"); a chart or number block you add later to a page that has a period block gets source.period: "page" too. addContainer {page, block} for the period block; updateContainer {page, block, changes: {source: {...}}} for each chart or number (to take one off the range, set source.period to null). Never leave the existing charts out and only offer to do it later: the user asked for the page to switch, so the charts switch. Changing the choices is updateContainer on the period block with changes {show: {options: [...]}}. A chart that follows the range ignores group.unit and last and picks day, week or month by the length of the range; with compare: "previous" it is drawn against the stretch right before (this week against last week, this month against last month); a number that follows ignores the inPeriod in its filter. A page has at most one period block. Pin it with pin: "top" if the user wants it to stay in view. Record blocks follow it too (list, cards, checklist, tiles, board, table, gallery): set source.period: "page" on every record block on that page, like the charts, unless the user says a list should stay as it is; a list that follows shows only the entries in the picked range, by the date field of the inPeriod in its filter (that inPeriod is then ignored) or else the first date field of the table. A calendar never follows (it moves by month), and a list with its own show.browse.period (rule 38) cannot follow too: keep the one the user asked for.
58. The entry itself on a page for one entry (rule 48): to show the opened entry's own fields there ("show the client's phone and address at the top") → a single block with source {table: the page's of table, record: "$record"} and show.fields the fields to show (a file field shows its pictures), usually first on the page, above the lists of what belongs to it. Its Edit button edits that entry. Without record it shows the oldest entry of the table, so never leave record out on such a page; never write record anywhere else.
59. Reminders some minutes before an entry's date and time ("remind me 30 minutes before each appointment") → when {before: {table, field: a datetime field of that table}, minutes} (1 to 10080: an hour = 60, a day = 1440; no at): one notification per entry, that many minutes before its date and time, with only the table name and the time in its text. It needs a datetime field (add one first if the table has only a date); for a date without a time use days and at (rule 35).
60. A daily or weekly reminder that stays quiet when it is already done ("remind me at 21:00 if I haven't logged anything today") → when {every: "day" or "week", …} with unless {table, within: "day" | "week" | "month", filter?, date?} (no link: there is no entry here): on a day whose day / week / month already has a matching entry in that table, it does not fire. The device plans the coming week ahead and plans again whenever entries change; nothing runs in the background. done and snoozeMinutes still only go with when.each.
61. Values a record tool takes from today or from this entry ("snooze a week", "renew for a year", "next review = today + this card's interval", "log it again", "order at today's price") → a date field takes {from: "today" or a date / datetime field of this entry, add: a whole number or a number field of this entry, unit: "days" | "months"} (negative add goes back; a month end clamps); any field may take {copy: a field of this entry}, copied when the user taps (same type, or number / money, or text / note; a link to the same table; formulas, lookups and rollups may be copied from, which freezes e.g. a price at order time, but never into); increment's by may be a number field of this entry. "This entry" is the entry the tool acts on ("$row": a row, tile or card tool, a reminder's done), or on a page for one entry the opened entry ("$record") for a button there. A button elsewhere, setAll and a form have no entry: only {from: "today", add: <number>} works there. Text is still never a constant (rule 44): to repeat a text, copy it. Examples: on the cards list {as: "button", label: "Good", do: "set", table: "cards", field: "due", value: {from: "today", add: "interval", unit: "days"}}; on the products list {as: "button", label: "Order", do: "create", table: "orders", values: {product: "$row", price: {copy: "price"}, qty: {copy: "usualQty"}}}.
62. One tap that changes two or three things of the same entry ("a Ship button that sets the status to shipped and the ship date to today", "a Done button that also logs a check-in for it") → on a row or tile tool (as "button" or "tap" on a record block) add also: 1 or 2 more writes on this entry, [{do: "set", field, value} | {do: "toggle", field} | {do: "increment", field, by}] (no table: it is this entry's table), and at most one {do: "create", table, values} whose link field is "$row". At most 3 writes in all; no ask, no setAll, no conditions inside; each field once. The app saves them together and offers Undo afterwards. Not on a page button, a form, a check or a drag, and never in a reminder's done (one change there). Example: {as: "button", label: "Ship", do: "set", table: "orders", field: "status", value: "shipped", when: [{field: "status", op: "isNot", value: "shipped"}], also: [{do: "set", field: "shippedOn", value: "today"}]}.
63. Creating one entry for each of several entries in one tap ("on the 1st, a button that creates this month's order for each regular customer", "add a task for every member") → a button block with tools [{do: "createAll", table: <the table to add to>, from: <the table to go through>, filter?: conditions on from, values}]: one new entry in table for every entry of from that matches the filter. In values, a link field pointing at from may be "$row" (that entry), and {copy: field} and {from: field, …} read that entry's fields (rule 61). The app asks first with the count, creates at most 200, and offers Undo for the whole batch. A required field without a default must be in values. Only on a button block (like setAll), never on a row or in a reminder's done. Example: {do: "createAll", table: "orders", from: "customers", filter: [{field: "regular", op: "is", value: true}], values: {customer: "$row", amount: {copy: "usualAmount"}, date: "today"}}.
64. Laying out the entry form of a table ("put the invoice fields in their own section that only shows when needs invoice is ticked", "quantity at least 1") → the entry editor stays Tinkrum's (saving, deleting, attachments, suggestions), but its layout is config, in four ways only: (1) sections: updateData on the table with changes {form: {sections: [{title?, fields: [fieldIds], when?}]}} (1-10 sections, each field in at most one; fields not named appear after the sections in table order, so a new field never needs listing); (2) when: 1-3 conditions (filter form, AND) on other stored fields of the same entry, never on a field inside that section; the section shows while they hold, live as the user types, and hiding clears nothing; (3) hint: a short text (≤80 chars) under one field's input, e.g. {op: "updateData", table, field, changes: {hint: "15 or 18 characters"}}, shown in the entry form and in form blocks; (4) min / max on a number, money or duration (minutes) field: a value outside is refused when it is saved, old values stay. These only arrange or check what the user types; never put entry data in a hint. Example: {op: "updateData", table: "orders", changes: {form: {sections: [{title: "Order", fields: ["item", "qty", "invoice"]}, {title: "Invoice", fields: ["taxNo", "company"], when: [{field: "invoice", op: "is", value: true}]}]}}}.
65. Tabs by a choice field on a page: when the user wants to switch a page between the options of one choice field ("tabs for To ship / Shipped / Done", "switch between statuses"), add ONE choices block {look: "choices", source: {table, field}} at the top of the page (pin: "top" if it should stay in view), with show.options only when the user names some of the options or an order, show.all: false only when they do not want "All", and show.default when they say which one opens first. Then set source.choice: "page" on EVERY list, cards, checklist, tiles, board, calendar, table, gallery, number and chart block on that page that reads the same table (all of them follow unless the user says one should stay as it is, e.g. "the total of all orders stays"); a block of that table you add later to such a page gets source.choice: "page" too. addContainer {page, block} for the choices block; updateContainer {page, block, changes: {source: {choice: "page"}}} for each block (to take one off, set source.choice to null). Never leave the existing blocks out and only offer to do it later. A block that reads another table cannot follow (leave it as it is). A block grouped by that same field (a board with a column per status, a pie or number grouped by it) already shows every option: leave it without source.choice; a list with show.browse.filter on that field keeps its own filter row instead (do not add both). A page has at most one choices block. It works next to a period block (rule 56): a block may follow both (source.period and source.choice both "page"). Adding right where you look (rule 45, values "$here") then starts the new entry with the picked option.
66. A reminder on a day of the month ("remind me on the 1st of every month to confirm my subscriptions") → when {every: "month", day: 1 to 28, at}. Days 29 to 31 do not exist in every month, so they are not offered: use 28 or say so in a note. The device plans the next few occurrences ahead and plans again whenever entries change or the app opens; nothing runs in the background, so a user who does not open the app for months gets no more until they do. It may carry unless {table, within: "month", filter?, date?} (rule 60, no link) to stay quiet in a month that already has a matching entry, e.g. unless {table: "payments", within: "month", filter: [{field: "subscription", op: "isNotEmpty"}]}. done and snoozeMinutes still only go with when.each.
67. Size of one block ("make this number smaller", "this title bigger") → style {size: "small" | "medium" | "large"} on that block, 0.85, 1 and 1.2 times. It scales the content of that block, not the space it takes and not other blocks: the text of a header, text, notice or callout, the icon and text of an entry tile, the number of a number block. Other blocks ignore it. "Bigger or smaller text everywhere" is still rule 11 (fontScale).
68. A check-in grid, rows × days ("see which habits I did this week", "attendance of each member per day", "which bills I paid each month") → a record block {look: "grid"} on the table that gets one entry each time something is done (check-ins, attendance, payments): source {table, group: {by: a link field (one row per entry of the linked table, e.g. each habit; group.filter on that table keeps e.g. only active ones) or a choice field (one row per option), showEmpty: true}, across: {unit: "day" | "week" | "month", by?: a date or datetime field (default the first date field), last?: 2-31 (default 7 days, 8 weeks, 6 months)}}, show {title: the title of the entries listed when a cell is opened}, tools [{as: "tap", do: "create", table, values: "$here"}, {as: "tap", do: "remove", table}] (no labels needed). Tapping an empty cell adds an entry for that row and that day (it needs no undo: tapping again takes it back); with remove, tapping a cell with exactly one entry moves it to Recently deleted and offers Undo, and a cell with two or more lists them. Leave remove out for counting ("8 glasses of water a day": every tap adds one more; show.format {kind: "progress", goal: a number, or a number field of the linked table such as each habit's daily goal} draws a ring; show.trailing, a number field, is summed instead of counted). remove exists only as this tap on a grid, never on a list, a button, a reminder's done or anywhere else. Add the table first when it is missing (a link field to the rows' table and a date field with default "today"). The newest column is the current day, week or month (weeks start as rule 41 sets); older cells can be filled in afterwards and there are no future columns.
69. Several options per entry ("which days I plan this meal on", "a book's genres", "the times of day this medicine is given", "light and humidity a plant needs") → a choice field with multiple: true; its options are fixed in the config like any choice, and an entry stores the ones picked. Use tags instead when the words are the user's own and not known in advance ("tag my notes"), and a link when each option is an entry of its own with more to it (a client, a project). Filters: is "mon" (or a list) keeps entries that have any of them, isNot keeps those that have none; grouping a list, cards, a number, a bar chart or a choices row by it puts an entry under every option it has, so the counts can add up to more than the entries. It can't be used in a formula, show.color, a pie chart, a board drag, a money currencyField or a previous within. Record tools write a list of option ids (["mon", "thu"]), which replaces what the entry had. Turning multiple on for an existing choice keeps every entry; turning it off is refused.
